court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: The court held that the Town of Inlet's 1966 zoning ordinance permitted short-term rental of a one-family dwelling in an R-1 district, entitling plaintiff to a declaration that his prior rentals were lawful, with a factual issue remaining on his nonconforming-use claim under the 2002 amendment. It further held plaintiff's property was not 'owner occupied' because he did not occupy any portion of it, and that the 2002 amendment restricting short-term rental of nonowner-occupied dwellings to protect neighborhood character was a valid, non-arbitrary exercise of the zoning power.

quotes.text: Construing the 1966 ordinance against defendant, plaintiff is entitled to a declaration that rental of his one-family dwelling for any time period was permitted under the original ordinance.
While short-term renting was not prohibited under the 1966 ordinance, it was clearly restricted in the amendment.
Finally, the amendment is not arbitrary, capricious or illegal.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: On a Labor Law §§ 240/241 homeowner-exemption dispute, the Appellate Division held that a worker injured while installing electrical service could proceed against the property owners because they failed to show the property was not being used solely for commercial purposes at the time of the accident. Their affidavits addressed only their intended residential use at purchase in 2004 and were silent on whether they continued using the property as a residence after they began operating a bed and breakfast there in 2008.

quotes.text: In or about January 2008, defendants began operating a bed and breakfast on the property with six guest rooms available for rental on weekends in January and February and four days each week from May to October.
That exemption, however, “is not available to an owner who uses or intends to use [the] dwelling only for commercial purposes”
we find that defendants failed to demonstrate their entitlement to the homeowners’ exemption as a matter of law
